subject: Jurisdictional routing & failover: private deployment runbook draft
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@greencloud.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment across EU + APAC — residency & failover questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We are evaluating Redwood Private for a multi-region deployment covering EU (GDPR-bound data) and APAC (Singapore + Japan). Key constraints: records generated in each region must remain within that region except for operational metadata, and we need a documented failover behavior with clear RTO/RPO for each region.

Questions to start:
- Is there a supported pattern for regional isolation (separate VPCs + per-region KV stores) with automated failover?
- How do you handle KMS keys and audit logs across borders?
- Can the control plane be run in our own VPC to satisfy sovereignty policies?

Can you share a short runbook or checklist so we can evaluate the gap vs our security/compliance policy?

Appreciate it — happy to set a call.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Infrastructure, GreenCloud
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@greencloud.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment across EU + APAC — residency & failover questions

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear constraints. Short answers up front and I’ll attach a draft runbook after we validate a few details.

- Yes: our recommended pattern for strict residency is per-region VPCs with customer-managed KMS keys in-region and async replication of non-personal operational data.
- KMS / audit logs: we support customer KMS (Bring Your Own Key) per region; audit logs can be kept in-region and exported to your SIEM.
- Control plane: we offer a private control plane option that can be deployed into your VPC (preferred for sovereign deployments).

To finalize the runbook we need: primary region for each workload, RTO/RPO targets per region, whether you require active-active or active-passive failover, and whether you want cross-region read replicas for low-latency reads.

If it helps, I’ve looped in Priyom (infrastructure) and Dylan (network) to propose a concrete design and a compact checklist. Can we do a 45-min design review tomorrow?

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Sr. PM, Private Deployments

Team — forwarding GreenCloud's ask. We need a concise runbook and an ops checklist they can use to decide whether to proceed with a pilot. Draft scope below — please keep responses short and actionable.

Scope (deliver by EOD tomorrow if possible):
- Minimal architecture pattern that meets ‘EU-only’ residency and APAC regional isolation.
- KMS mapping: customer-key per-region mapping and wrap/unwrap flow.
- Network failover behavior: DNS, load balancer, and transit gateway actions for failover.
- RTO/RPO examples for active-passive (cold standby) vs active-active (replicas).
- List of artifacts they need to provide (VPC CIDRs, firewall rules, KMS ARNs, auditors contact).

Questions I need answered in the doc:
1) Do we recommend active-active for GreenCloud’s use case (global read latency vs stronger legal controls)?
2) Who owns the control-plane components in the private delivery? Redwood or customer? (we support both; prefer customer-managed for sovereign).

Priyom — can you take ownership of the runbook draft? Dylan — network section + diagram. Lauren — include compliance checklist and DPA callouts. Markus — pricing/ops impact note for an active-active design.

Thanks — Soojin

Quick technical summary / proposal notes (for the runbook):

Recommended baseline architecture:
- Per-region customer VPCs (EU: eu-west-1 + optional eu-central-1; APAC: ap-southeast-1 (SG), ap-northeast-1 (JP)).
- Deploy Redwood Private runtime in each region inside the customer's VPC (customer-managed control plane).
- Storage strategy: region-scoped data buckets/volumes for personal data (encrypted with customer KMS in-region). Non-personal operational data can replicate to a centralized ops bucket subject to their policy.
- Replication model: async cross-region replication for non-sensitive assets; for user data, use replication only where allowed (explicit consent or binding safeguards).

Failover patterns (recommended):
1) Active-passive (default):
   - Primary region processes writes. Standby region holds encrypted snapshots and warmed read-only replicas.
   - RPO: nightly snapshots + 15-min incremental logs => RPO ~ 15m (configurable).
   - RTO: DNS + LB cutover + cache warm => 5-15 min for service endpoints, 10-30 min for full state reconciliation.
2) Active-active (only if customer accepts cross-border replication):
   - Dual-write to region-local stores with conflict resolution at application level or strong coordination layer.
   - Lower read latency globally but increases regulatory risk if personal data is replicated.

KMS & Audit logs:
- Use customer KMS keys (BYOK) per region; keys never leave region. We support envelope encryption where root key stays in-region and our runtime holds only ephemeral data keys (wrapped).
- Audit logs are delivered to a customer-owned S3 (or equivalent) bucket per region via an in-region collector. Log forwarding to a centralized SIEM can be done over an encrypted, auditable pipeline if customer authorizes it.

Networking / DNS failover:
- Use regional load balancers + health checks. Prefer DNS-based failover with short TTLs (30s) and pre-warmed endpoints. Route53 or Cloudflare can be used.
- For predictable egress and peering, recommend Transit Gateway/Interconnect with BGP for deterministic failover. Avoid cross-region VPC peering for sovereignty reasons.

Constraints & compliance notes:
- GDPR: so-called 'EU-only' data must remain in EU unless adequate safeguards (SCCs, DPA amendment) are in place.
- Japan/Singapore: APAC jurisdictions have different definitions of sensitive data; treat them as region-scoped unless customer instructs otherwise.

I will assemble these into a short runbook PDF and attach the diagram. Priyom
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-04T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Private deployment across EU + APAC — network diagram + draft runbook

Attaching the initial network diagram and a compact runbook draft. Key network decisions called out in the doc:
- Transit topology: customer TGW per region with an edge transit hosted in a single APAC/EU colo for routing (diagram attached).
- DNS plan: split-horizon DNS — internal endpoints resolve to private IPs; external resolve to regional LB endpoints. Health checks to trigger DNS failover.
- BGP: advertise primary prefix from primary region; standby region advertises only when session established post-failover to avoid asymmetric routing.

Attachment stubs:
- network-diagram-eu-apac.vsdx (Visio)
- 20261004-jurisdictional-runbook-draft.pdf (PDF)

Notes: pre-warm capacity in the standby region to reduce RTO — small cost but important for SLA-driven customers. Dylan

Dylan Brooks
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emma — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise runbook and network diagram that reflect the team’s recommendation. TL;DR: start with an active-passive setup (region-scoped data buckets + customer-managed KMS per region) and a documented failover play (DNS cutover + BGP route announcement from standby). We recommend pre-warming the standby region and agreeing RTO/RPO targets in the pilot.

What we attached: 20261004-jurisdictional-runbook-draft.pdf — runbook with checklist and required artifacts (VPC CIDRs, KMS ARNs, auditor contact).
network-diagram-eu-apac.vsdx — visual topology for TGW/BGP/DNS.
compliance-evidence-bundle.zip — examples of how audit logs and key usage records can be captured per region.

Next steps we propose:
1) Sign the DPA addendum for cross-region operational metadata export (if needed).
2) Customer provides VPC CIDRs, firewall egress list, KMS ARNs, and the primary region mapping per workload.
3) Schedule a 90-min pilot kickoff next week to provision a pre-warmed standby and run a failover drill.

Please let me know if you want any of the sections expanded; we can trim the runbook for the security team or expand into a full runbook for SRE. Happy to set the pilot date after sign-off.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
